message.content:
Below is a **sample “Startup Stats” API** that you can use as a reference or prototype for your own service.  
It follows a REST‑style design, accepts a few query parameters, and returns JSON (or XML if you prefer).  

---

## 1. API Endpoint

```
GET https://api.example.com/v1/startups/stats
```

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Description                                                                 |
|-----------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `country` | string | ISO‑3166‑1 alpha‑2 country code (e.g., `US`, `GB`, `DE`). Optional.        |
| `industry` | string | Industry slug (e.g., `fintech`, `healthtech`). Optional.                    |
| `min_funding` | number | Minimum total funding in USD. Optional.                                     |
| `max_funding` | number | Maximum total funding in USD. Optional.                                     |
| `format` | enum (`json`, `xml`) | Desired response format. Default is `json`. |

> **Note**: The API is rate‑limited to 100 requests per minute per IP address.

---

## 2. Sample Request

```http
GET https://api.example.com/v1/startups/stats?country=US&industry=fintech&min_funding=5000000&format=json HTTP/1.1
Accept: application/json
```

---

## 3. Sample Response (JSON)

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "count": 3,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 50,
    "total_pages": 1
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "startup_001",
      "name": "FinTech Innovators",
      "country": "US",
      "industry": "fintech",
      "funding_total_usd": 12000000,
      "funding_rounds": 4,
      "employees": 45,
      "founded_year": 2015,
      "website": "https://www.fintechinnovators.com",
      "description": "A platform that simplifies cross‑border payments."
    },
    {
      "id": "startup_002",
      "name": "HealthPay Solutions",
      "country": "US",
      "industry": "fintech",
      "funding_total_usd": 8500000,
      "funding_rounds": 3,
      "employees": 30,
      "founded_year": 2017,
      "website": "https://www.healthpaysolutions.com",
      "description": "Secure payment gateway for healthcare providers."
    },
    {
      "id": "startup_003",
      "name": "CryptoLedger",
      "country": "US",
      "industry": "fintech",
      "funding_total_usd": 6500000,
      "funding_rounds": 2,
      "employees": 25,
      "founded_year": 2018,
      "website": "https://www.cryptledger.com",
      "description": "Blockchain‑based ledger for financial institutions."
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 4. Sample Response (XML)

```xml
<response>
  <meta>
    <count>3</count>
    <page>1</page>
    <per_page>50</per_page>
    <total_pages>1</total_pages>
  </meta>
  <data>
    <startup>
      <id>startup_001</id>
      <name>FinTech Innovators</name>
      <country>US</country>
      <industry>fintech</industry>
      <funding_total_usd>12000000</funding_total_usd>
      <funding_rounds>4</funding_rounds>
      <employees>45</employees>
      <founded_year>2015</founded_year>
      <website>https://www.fintechinnovators.com</website>
      <description>A platform that simplifies cross‑border payments.</description>
    </startup>
    <!-- ... other startups ... -->
  </data>
</response>
```

---

## 5. How to Call the API Using the Provided `requests_get` Function

```python
from functions import requests_get

response = requests_get({
    "url": "https://api.example.com/v1/startups/stats",
    "params": {
        "country": "US",
        "industry": "fintech",
        "min_funding": 5000000,
        "format": "json"
    },
    "headers": {
        "Accept": "application/json"
    },
    "timeout": 10.0
})

print(response)
```

> **Tip**: If you need authentication (e.g., an API key), add it to the `headers`:

```python
"headers": {
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

---

## 6. Extending the API

| Feature | How to Add |
|---------|------------|
| Pagination | Add `page` and `per_page` query params. |
| Sorting | Add `sort_by` (e.g., `funding_total_usd`) and `order` (`asc`/`desc`). |
| Aggregations | Add `aggregate=true` to return totals, averages, etc. |
| Webhooks | Provide a `webhook_url` param to receive push notifications on new funding rounds. |

---

### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Define the data model (fields, types, units).
- [ ] Decide on authentication (API key, OAuth, etc.).
- [ ] Implement rate limiting and caching.
- [ ] Provide clear error responses (400, 401, 429, 500).
- [ ] Write documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger) for developers.

Feel free to adapt the above skeleton to your own data sources (Crunchbase, AngelList, PitchBook, etc.) or to expose your internal startup database. If you need help wiring this up to a real data source or generating a Swagger spec, let me know!
